introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0580 Physics 1, June 2025, Ordinary Level). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. No physical constants are printed on the paper except $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$ in Question 26.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-42) has independent questions; Section II (questions 43-50) has two groups of questions about practical situations (Questions 43-46 and 47-50).

Four graphs of y (vertical axis) against x (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A falling straight line, B curve rising more and more steeply, C falling curve flattening out, D rising straight line through the origin (Question 20).

Four graphs of resistance R (vertical axis) against length l (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A horizontal line, B rising straight line through the origin, C falling straight line, D curve rising more and more steeply (Question 23).
Two conducting bodies drawn as boxes: A marked +200 V and B marked -100 V (Question 25).

Four graphs of frequency f (vertical axis) against speed v (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A falling curve, B horizontal line, C curve rising then flattening out, D rising straight line through the origin (Question 28).
Resistors of 1 ohm and 2 ohms connected in parallel, in series with a 6 V battery of negligible internal resistance (Question 33).
Voltage (V) against time (t) graph of an a.c. source: sine wave of amplitude 20 V, zero crossings with the time axis marked at 0.04 s and 0.08 s, two complete cycles by 0.08 s (Question 34).
Ray of light reflected by a plane surface with the normal drawn; the angle of 25 degrees is marked between the incident ray and the surface (Question 36).
Simple circuit: a cell, an ammeter A in the main loop, a resistor R, and a voltmeter V connected in parallel across R (Question 39).

Q4 : « quality » d'un son = timbre, donc les harmoniques (overtones) ; réponse D.
Q11 : « solar panel » retenu comme capteur solaire thermique (lumière vers chaleur) ; une « solar cell » donne de l'électricité.

Les 11 figures ont été découpées dans les pages rendues sans filigrane (scan en régime B_cuit, filtre de niveaux appliqué), contrôle OCR OK. Sur la figure 11 de l'original, le point D apparaît deux fois (sommet et fin de la descente) ; recopié tel quel.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 46.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following quantities is constant for a body falling freely near the earth's surface?
questions.corrige_markdown: A body falling freely is acted on by gravity only, so its acceleration is the constant acceleration of free fall $g$ near the Earth's surface. Its velocity increases, so its kinetic energy and its linear momentum $mv$ both increase; air resistance is not constant either (it grows with speed, and it is ignored in free fall). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Anything that can do work is said to possess:
questions.corrige_markdown: Energy is defined as the capacity (ability) to do work. Force is a push or a pull, efficiency is a ratio of useful output to input, and power is the rate of doing work. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following electromagnetic waves can be used to detect fake bank notes?
questions.corrige_markdown: Genuine bank notes carry security marks printed with fluorescent ink. Under ultra-violet light these marks glow, whereas forged notes usually do not, so ultra-violet rays are used in note detectors. Gamma rays and X-rays are far too penetrating and harmful for this use, and infra-red rays do not make ink fluoresce. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The quality of a sound wave is determined by the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The quality (timbre) of a note is what makes the same note sound different on a flute and on a guitar. It depends on the number and relative strength of the overtones mixed with the fundamental, that is on the shape of the waveform. Frequency fixes the pitch and amplitude fixes the loudness. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The focal length of a convex lens is 10 cm. When an object is placed 15 cm from the lens, the image formed is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The object distance $u = 15\ \mathrm{cm}$ lies between $f = 10\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $2f = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$. Using $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30}$, so $v = 30\ \mathrm{cm}$ (positive, so the image is real). The magnification is $\dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{30}{15} = 2 > 1$, so the image is magnified (and inverted). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why does alcohol give a cooling effect when poured on a body?
questions.corrige_markdown: Alcohol evaporates quickly from the skin. To change from liquid to vapour its molecules need latent heat of vaporization, which they take from the skin, so the skin cools. Option B has the energy flowing the wrong way. A and D describe properties of alcohol, but they do not explain the cooling by themselves. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It sends out latent heat of vaporization to the body
It absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the body
It has a low boiling point

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in Figure 1 shows how the temperature ($\Theta$) of a pure melting substance varies with the quantity of heat energy (Q) absorbed by the substance?

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: While a pure substance melts, the heat absorbed is used to break the bonds between the particles (latent heat of fusion) and not to raise the temperature, so the temperature stays constant: the graph of $\Theta$ against $Q$ is a horizontal line. This is graph C. Graph A has a falling temperature, B a steadily rising temperature (heating with no change of state) and D a rising curve. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Alternating current which has not been rectified is not suitable for:
questions.corrige_markdown: Charging a battery needs a current that always flows in the same direction (direct current), because a battery stores energy by a chemical change that must go one way. Unrectified a.c. reverses direction and would not charge it properly. An electromagnet, a filament bulb (heating effect) and a motor-driven grinding machine all work on a.c. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Images formed by concave lenses are always:
questions.corrige_markdown: A concave (diverging) lens makes the refracted rays spread out, so they never meet: the image is always virtual, upright and diminished, wherever the object is. So the only correct option is virtual. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following quantities has the unit $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$?
questions.corrige_markdown: Momentum $= mv$ has the unit $\mathrm{kg \times m\,s^{-1}} = \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. Density is $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, force is $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$ (newton) and a moment is $\mathrm{N\,m} = \mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these transducers converts light to heat energy?
questions.corrige_markdown: A transducer changes energy from one form to another. A solar panel (a solar water heater) absorbs sunlight and turns it into heat. A filament bulb changes electrical energy into light and heat, a solar cell changes light into electrical energy, and a wind turbine changes kinetic energy into electrical energy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If air is pumped into a ball on a cold day, on a hot day the mass and density will:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pumping air in adds air to the ball, so the mass of air inside increases. The ball is rigid, so its volume is (almost) unchanged. Density $= \dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$ therefore increases too. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Mass: remains the same; Density: increase
Mass: remain the same; Density: decrease

questions.enonce_markdown: An electrical device is rated 60 W, 240 V. The current drawn by the device when it is operating is:
questions.corrige_markdown: From $P = IV$: $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{60\ \mathrm{W}}{240\ \mathrm{V}} = 0.25\ \mathrm{A}$. Option A is the wrong ratio $V/P$ inverted ($240/60 = 4$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these fuses is ideal for use in a shaving machine rated 240 V, 1100 W?
questions.corrige_markdown: Normal current $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1100}{240} = 4.58\ \mathrm{A}$. The fuse must have a rating just above the normal current, so that it does not blow in normal use but protects the appliance: 5 A. A 4 A fuse would blow at once, 4.6 A is too close to the working value, and 218 A would never protect the device. (218 A is far too high to protect the appliance.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A rifle fires a bullet and recoils. The recoil velocity of the rifle is less than the velocity of the bullet because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Momentum is conserved: before firing the total momentum is zero, so $m_\mathrm{b}v_\mathrm{b} = m_\mathrm{r}v_\mathrm{r}$ (in opposite directions). The two momenta have equal size, so $v_\mathrm{r} = \dfrac{m_\mathrm{b}}{m_\mathrm{r}}\,v_\mathrm{b}$ is small because $m_\mathrm{r} \gg m_\mathrm{b}$. Option B is false (the momenta are equal in size), and D is false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the recoil velocity is opposite to the velocity of the bullet
the momentum of the bullet is greater than the momentum of the rifle
the mass of the rifle is much greater than the mass of the bullet
the law of conservation of linear momentum does not hold

questions.enonce_markdown: A razor blade is observed to be used to cut a piece of cloth with more ease than with a knife. This could be explained most precisely by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pressure $= \dfrac{F}{A}$. The edge of a razor blade is much thinner than that of a knife, so for the same force the area of contact is very small and the pressure on the cloth is very high, which cuts it easily. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: small area of contact and small force exerted
high pressure and high force exerted
small area of contact and high pressure exerted
small force and low pressure exerted

questions.enonce_markdown: A boy lifts a bag of beans with a force of 40 N through a vertical height of 2 m in 4 s. The power developed by the boy is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Work done $= F \times d = 40 \times 2 = 80\ \mathrm{J}$. Power $= \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{80}{4} = 20\ \mathrm{W}$. Option B is the work (forgetting to divide by time). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following natural occurrences is due to the fact that light travels in a straight line?
questions.corrige_markdown: A shadow forms because light travels in straight lines and cannot bend round an opaque object. An echo is a reflection of sound, a rainbow is caused by refraction and dispersion of sunlight in raindrops, and a mirage is caused by the refraction of light in layers of air of different density. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 600 000 J of energy is used to heat 2 kg of water of specific heat capacity $4200\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}K^{-1}}$. The temperature rise produced is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $Q = mc\Delta\theta$, so $\Delta\theta = \dfrac{Q}{mc} = \dfrac{600\,000}{2 \times 4200} = \dfrac{600\,000}{8400} = 71.4\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 2 best shows the relationship between the extension of a spring (y) and the force applied (x) when Hooke's law is obeyed?

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Hooke's law says that the extension is directly proportional to the applied force (as long as the limit of proportionality is not exceeded). The graph of extension $y$ against force $x$ is therefore a straight line through the origin with a positive gradient. This is graph D. A is a falling straight line, B and C are curves. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following does NOT affect the speed of sound in air?
questions.corrige_markdown: The speed of sound in air increases with temperature and with humidity (moist air is less dense), and a wind carries the sound along or against its direction. A change of pressure at constant temperature changes the density in the same proportion, so it has no effect on the speed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How does the conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor vary with an increase in temperature?
questions.corrige_markdown: In an intrinsic (pure) semiconductor, a rise in temperature gives more electrons enough energy to leave their bonds, so more charge carriers (electrons and holes) are free to move. The conductivity increases (unlike in a metal, where the resistance rises with temperature). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in Figure 3 shows how the resistance (R) of a copper wire of uniform cross-sectional area, varies with its length ($\ell$)?

![fig-3](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: For a wire of uniform cross-section, $R = \dfrac{\rho \ell}{A}$, so $R$ is directly proportional to the length $\ell$. The graph is a straight line through the origin, graph B. A would mean $R$ is independent of length, C a resistance that falls as the wire gets longer, and D a curve. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the elastic limit of a wire is not exceeded, then the wire:
questions.corrige_markdown: Below the elastic limit the wire returns to its original length when the load is removed. While stretched it stores elastic potential energy, which it gives back (converted into other forms such as kinetic energy) when released. Option B is only guaranteed up to the limit of proportionality, which can be lower than the elastic limit; C is not a general property and D describes a spring balance. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: can store and convert elastic potential energy to other forms of energy
can be easily stretched and compressed
can be used to measure force

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 4 shows two charged bodies A and B.

![fig-4](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

If the two conductors are linked using a conducting wire, charges will flow from A to B until:
questions.corrige_markdown: Charge flows between two conductors because of a potential difference (here $+200\ \mathrm{V}$ on A and $-100\ \mathrm{V}$ on B). It stops only when the two conductors are at the same potential, i.e. when there is no potential difference. They are not necessarily left with equal charges (this depends on their sizes) and they are not necessarily discharged. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: there are equal number of charges on A and B
there is an equal amount of energy on A and B
A and B are completely discharged
there is no difference in potential between A and B

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, then the number of electrons on a polythene rod which carries a charge of 32 C is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Number of electrons $n = \dfrac{Q}{e} = \dfrac{32}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 20 \times 10^{19} = 2 \times 10^{20}$. Option C is wrong by a factor of 10, and A and B have the wrong sign of the exponent (they come from multiplying instead of dividing). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The mechanical advantage of a machine is 3 and the velocity ratio is 4. What is the efficiency of the machine?
questions.corrige_markdown: $\text{Efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{MA}}{\text{VR}} \times 100\% = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 100\% = 75\%$. Options A and B are the ratios $0.75$ and $1.33$ without the factor $100$ (or inverted), and D is the inverted ratio ($4/3 = 133\%$, impossible for a machine). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 5 shows how the frequency (f) of a wave varies with the speed (v) of the wave as it moves into deeper water?

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: When a water wave moves into deeper water its speed and wavelength change, but its frequency is fixed by the source and does not change. So $f$ stays constant whatever the value of $v$: a horizontal line, graph B. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The unit of electric current is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The SI unit of current is the ampere (A). The coulomb is the unit of charge, the volt of potential difference and the ohm of resistance. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the energy sources below is renewable?
questions.corrige_markdown: A renewable source is replaced naturally as fast as it is used. Solar energy comes from the Sun continuously. Coal and petrol (fossil fuels) took millions of years to form, and the uranium used in nuclear power stations is a limited resource. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An object falling from a great height will attain terminal velocity when:
questions.corrige_markdown: As the object speeds up, the air resistance (drag) grows until it equals the weight. The resultant (net) force is then zero, so the acceleration is zero and the object keeps a constant speed, the terminal velocity. Air resistance and the weight both still act, so A and C are false, and the acceleration then is zero, not constant at $g$. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: no air resistance force acts on it
no force acts on the body
the net force on the body is zero

questions.enonce_markdown: When a rubber catapult is stretched and released, it throws a stone of mass 0.02 kg at a speed of $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The kinetic energy of the stone is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $\mathrm{KE} = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 0.02 \times 10^{2} = 1\ \mathrm{J}$. Option A comes from forgetting the factor $\tfrac12$ ($0.02 \times 100 = 2$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 6 shows a network of two resistors connected to a battery of negligible internal resistance.

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

The p.d across the the $2\ \Omega$ resistor is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The $1\ \Omega$ and $2\ \Omega$ resistors are connected in parallel directly across the 6 V battery, whose internal resistance is negligible. Resistors in parallel have the same p.d. as the supply, so the p.d. across the $2\ \Omega$ resistor is 6 V. (The current in it is $6/2 = 3\ \mathrm{A}$; the values 4 V and 2 V come from wrongly treating the resistors as being in series, which would give $\tfrac{2}{3} \times 6 = 4\ \mathrm{V}$ across the $2\ \Omega$ resistor.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 7 shows a voltage (V) against time (t) graph of an a.c source.

![fig-7](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

The frequency of the source is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The graph passes through two complete cycles in 0.08 s (it starts at 0 and returns to zero going upward at 0.04 s, and again at 0.08 s). One period is therefore $T = 0.04\ \mathrm{s}$, and $f = \dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1}{0.04} = 25\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Option B is the time for two cycles, not a frequency. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In cold weather, a piece of iron feels colder than a piece of wood when touched because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Both objects are at the same temperature (that of the surroundings). Iron is a good conductor, so it carries heat away from the hand quickly and the hand loses heat faster: the iron feels colder. Wood is a poor conductor (an insulator) and removes heat slowly. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: iron is at a lower temperature than wood
wood is a better emitter of heat than iron
iron is a better conductor of heat than wood
iron is smooth while wood is rough

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 8 shows a ray of light reflected by a plane surface.

![fig-8](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

The angle of reflection is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The $25^\circ$ marked is the angle between the incident ray and the surface, not the angle with the normal. The angle of incidence is measured from the normal: $i = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$. By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection $r = i = 65^\circ$. Option A is the trap of using the angle with the surface. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: John uses 10 s to lift a box from the floor onto a table while Peter uses 25 s to do the same thing. Which of the following is correct?
questions.corrige_markdown: Both lift the same box through the same height, so they do the same work $W = mgh$ (A and B are false). Power is the rate of doing work, $P = \dfrac{W}{t}$: John takes less time, so his power is greater. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: John does more work than Peter
John does less work than Peter
John has more power than Peter
John has less power than Peter

questions.enonce_markdown: The setting up of a voltage across a wire which is experiencing a change in magnetic flux is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Producing an e.m.f. (voltage) in a conductor when the magnetic flux linked with it changes is the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law). Magnetization and demagnetization concern magnetic materials, and "induction" alone is not specific (there is also electrostatic induction). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 9 shows a simple electric circuit

![fig-9](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)

Which of the following correctly classifies the resistor (R), voltmeter (V) and ammeter (A) in order of increasing resistance?
questions.corrige_markdown: An ammeter is connected in series so it must have a very low resistance. A voltmeter is connected in parallel with the component so it must have a very high resistance, so that it draws almost no current. The resistor R has a resistance in between. In order of increasing resistance: ammeter, resistor, voltmeter. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following elements is a semiconducting material?
questions.corrige_markdown: Silicon (like germanium) is a semiconducting element. Phosphorus is a non-metal used as a donor impurity (dopant) in silicon, not a semiconductor itself in this context. A diode and a filament bulb are devices, not elements. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A woman is treated of a disease in the thyroid gland using radioactive iodine-131. Which device could be used to monitor the progress of the iodine-131?
questions.corrige_markdown: Iodine-131 emits radiation that can be detected outside the body. A Geiger-Muller (G-M) tube detects ionising radiation and gives a count rate, so it can follow the iodine in the thyroid. A manometer measures pressure, a thermometer temperature, and a cathode ray oscilloscope displays voltage waveforms. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 10 shows a coil XY connected to a d.c supply.

![fig-10](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_10.png)

The polarities of X and Y are
questions.corrige_markdown: The battery symbol has its long plate (positive) on the left, and the arrows in the figure show the current leaving the battery to the left, going up to X, through the coil from X to Y and back down at Y. On the front side of the turns the current flows downwards. Applying the right-hand grip rule (fingers along the current, thumb gives the direction of the field inside the coil) the field inside the coil points to the right, towards Y. The end where the field lines leave is a north pole, so Y is N; viewed from X the current is clockwise, which is a south pole, so X is S. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 43 - 46

The graph in figure 11 carries some information of the motion of a car of mass 1000 kg moving on a straight road. Use the information on the graph to answer questions 43 to 46.

![fig-11](gce-ol-physics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_11.png)

The distance covered by the car over the interval represented by AB is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Between A ($t = 0$) and B ($t = 20\ \mathrm{s}$) the graph is horizontal at $v = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Distance = area under the graph $= 20 \times 20 = 400\ \mathrm{m}$. Option A is $20 \times 10$ (wrong time), B is the sum $20 + 20$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For how long does the car move with constant velocity during the journey?
questions.corrige_markdown: The velocity is constant only along AB, where the line is horizontal, from $t = 0$ to $t = 20\ \mathrm{s}$: that is 20 s. After B the velocity increases up to 30 s and then decreases to zero at 40 s. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Over which interval is the acceleration zero?
questions.corrige_markdown: The acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph. The gradient is zero where the line is horizontal, which is the interval AB (constant velocity). Along the next two straight parts of the graph, the gradient is not zero. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The force necessary to cause the car to come to rest is:

*Options as printed:* A) - 4000 N   B) - 1000 N   C) 1000 N   D) 4000 N
questions.corrige_markdown:
The car comes to rest in the last part of the graph, from $40\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t = 30\ \mathrm{s}$ to $0$ at $t = 40\ \mathrm{s}$. Acceleration $= \dfrac{0 - 40}{40 - 30} = -4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Force $F = ma = 1000 \times (-4) = -4000\ \mathrm{N}$: the retarding force has a magnitude of 4000 N and acts opposite to the motion. The negative sign in the options is the direction, so the printed options A (-4000 N) and D (4000 N) are both defensible, depending on whether the sign is meant.

**Intended answer: A (- 4000 N).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 47 - 50

The equation below represents a reaction carried out in a nuclear reactor.

$$
^{235}_{92}\mathrm{U} + {}^{1}_{0}\mathrm{n} \rightarrow {}^{143}_{P}\mathrm{X} + {}^{Q}_{36}\mathrm{Y} + \text{Energy}
$$

The number 235 represents:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the notation $^{A}_{Z}\mathrm{X}$ the upper number is the mass number $A$ (the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus) and the lower number is the atomic number $Z$ (number of protons). So 235 is the mass number of uranium-235 (and 92 is its atomic number). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process described by the equation is:
